_doc: Beaten to 0 health in a street fight is beaten senseless, not dead (systems/knockout.js). npc: how long a knocked-out townsperson lies senseless (seconds, [min, max]; a real minute is an hour) and the share of health they wake with. player: hours lost when the player is knocked out, the health share they wake with, and the share of their purse taken when robbed. finish: the chance whoever downed the player finishes them — base, a violent (aggressive) sort, one who dislikes them (disposition under 25, added), one holding a grudge (the player hurt their kin or friend), one whose kin the player killed; the watch never kills (it arrests the wanted). rob: the chance, by role, they go through the player's purse instead of just leaving. Who started it matters: fetchWatch — the player threw the first blow, so (in a town with a watch) the one who downed them runs for the guards, with this chance, and the player wakes in the cells (unless a grudge finishes them first). npcStarted — they set on the player: finish (by temperament: base/aggressive/grudge) or, where the realm allows it, capture into their own prison camp (capture: the chance; days: [min, max] of labour; freedomCost: gold per day left), else rob or leave. privatePrisons: whether a realm lets private citizens keep prison camps and prisoners to work — allowShare of realms do (picked by a hash of the realm, the same all game), unless a realm's laws.privatePrisons says otherwise. householder: someone at home who hates the player (a grudge, or disposition under hateBelow; aggressive temperament under angryBelow) may set on them when they walk in (chance, once a visit). lines: what they say ({victim} = the one the grudge is for, {camp} = the camp's name).

arrest: That's enough. You're coming with me.
warn: Let that be a lesson. Stay out of trouble.
fetch: Stay there — I'm fetching the watch.
You'll answer to the watch for this.
capture: You'll make a fine pair of hands for {camp}.
Chain this one. To {camp} with them.
householder: I know what you did. You'll not leave here standing.
Get out — no. You're not getting out.
